subject: Order Form: pricing fallback matrix & invoice mapping
messages:
From: Matt Hughes <matt.hughes@acmecloud.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmecloud.com>, Elena Sosa <elena@fortis-legal.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form questions — invoice mapping and fallback behavior

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for sending the order form. Our legal team has a couple of open items on the pricing exhibits before procurement can sign: primarily the interplay between the pricing caps/floors and the proposed fallback model matrix. We want to understand how usage will be billed if Redwood automatically switches to a lower-cost model variant during capacity constraints (the "fallback").

Specific asks:
- Can you add an explicit mapping in the exhibit that ties token metrics on the invoice to the model variant charged (e.g., StandardModel-A = token-rate X; FallbackModel-B = token-rate Y)?
- How do caps/floors interact with fallback in a month where the customer's aggregate token spend crosses a cap threshold mid-month? Is there a pro-rata true-up or is the cap applied at billing period close?
- We attached a redline (Acme_Orderform_v1_redline.pdf) with comments — some of the language on "stabilization corridors" looks like it could be interpreted two ways.

Can your team propose concrete wording that maps the invoice line items to model variants and clarifies the cap/floor true-up behavior? If easier, a short fallback matrix (spreadsheet) would help.

We'd like to close these before EOD Friday so procurement can route for signature next week.

Thanks,
Matt Hughes\Director, Cloud Platform Procurement\AcmeCloud

Attachments: Acme_Orderform_v1_redline.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Matt Hughes <matt.hughes@acmecloud.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoice mapping and fallback behavior

Matt — thanks, and appreciate the quick turnaround.

High-level response first, then next steps:
- We agree that invoice mapping should be explicit. I'll attach a fallback matrix that maps our billing SKU/line-item to the model variant and per-token price. The matrix will also include a short rule for intra-period true-ups.
- For caps/floors crossing mid-month: our standard approach is to compute the billing tier at invoice close and true-up the applied unit price for the whole period based on aggregate usage (i.e., no retroactive re-rating of earlier invoices within the same billing period). However, we can offer a pro-rata alternative in the order form as an optional clause (usually requires a small fee to cover accounting complexity).
- For the "stabilization corridor" wording: Laura + Marissa, can you propose phrasing that unambiguously states (a) customer billed per-token based on model variant used to serve token, and (b) Redwood will report any mid-period fallback events with a daily digest in the Console?

I'll attach the initial fallback matrix and a short draft clause. If that looks good to Acme, we can fold into the order form and push a clean execution copy.

Proposed next steps:
1) Review matrix I attach and confirm token-to-line-item mapping (Matt).
2) Laura/Marissa: provide redline language for the exhibit by EOD.
3) Karthik/Rishi: prepare a mutually acceptable pro-rata true-up option and note the accounting impact.

Thanks — aiming to close Friday.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer\Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference\Phone: +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: pricing_fallback_matrix_v2.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Matt Hughes <matt.hughes@acmecloud.com>, Elena Sosa <elena@fortis-legal.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 13:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoice mapping and fallback behavior

Team — read the redline and Karthik's note. Below is proposed exhibit language (high level) that I will port into a formal markup: 

1) Invoice mapping: 
"Each invoice line item will reference a Redwood billing SKU and list the Model Variant assigned for that SKU during the billing period. Usage will be measured in billable tokens. If multiple model variants are used in the period, Redwood will aggregate token totals per model variant and invoice each at the applicable per-token rate for that variant."

2) Fallback & true-up: 
"If Redwood's runtime routing policy routes requests to a fallback Model Variant due to capacity management, outage mitigation, or regional routing ("Fallback Event"), Redwood will: (a) tag affected requests and include a daily event digest in the Console for the Customer; (b) invoice usage by model variant as measured; and (c) apply pricing caps/floors on an aggregate-period basis at invoice close. For Customers electing the Pro-Rata True-Up option, Redwood will instead apply cap thresholds pro-rated over the billing period according to the time-weighted share of each rate band, subject to an administration fee set forth in the Order Form."

3) Reporting/Transparency: 
"Redwood will provide a fallback report (CSV) with token breakdown by model variant for each billing period on request, and will retain routing logs for ninety (90) days for audit purposes."

Comments:
- Laura: I kept the fallback digest + CSV reporting requirement for transparency.
- Rishi: need to add a short definition for "billing SKU" and confirm the language around "invoice close" (EOM by default).

I can convert this into a tracked-change PDF if Acme's counsel wants markup.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole\Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Matt Hughes <matt.hughes@acmecloud.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, Elena Sosa <elena@fortis-legal.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoice mapping and fallback behavior

Matt — looping you back with the concrete language Marissa proposed and the updated matrix attached. Key points to confirm so we can turn the redline to clean: 
- Will Acme accept aggregate-period cap application (invoice-close true-up) as the default, with Pro-Rata True-Up as a selectable option on the front page of the Order Form?
- Is the daily fallback digest + monthly CSV report sufficient for your audit/finance team, or do you need streaming logs pushed to a shared S3 bucket? (That is technically feasible but adds an integration step.)

If you can confirm on these two items today, we'll incorporate and circulate a final redline. Proposed meeting: 11:00 AM PT today if you want to walk through the matrix live.

Thanks —Karthik

Karthik/Marissa/Laura — appreciate the quick work and clear language. Acme is comfortable with the default aggregate-period cap true-up, and we will take the Pro-Rata True-Up as an optional add-on (please add the administration fee language and checkbox on page 1). For reporting: the daily digest + monthly CSV is sufficient for now — we may request S3 delivery later but that's out-of-scope for signature this week.

Please fold Marissa's language into the order form redline and send us a clean copy for signature. We expect procurement to route internally on Monday.

Matt
Director, Cloud Platform Procurement\AcmeCloud
